claim: TypeSafe's homepage headline is 'up to 193.6x faster, up to 444.6x cheaper.' The xArm7 repository is the only place in this ecosystem that publishes a matched, independently replayable head-to-head with per-call costs and per-call model wait times for both sides. Read against it, the cost multiplier is roughly the right order of magnitude and the speed multiplier is not: the measured per-call latency ratio is 4.57x, about 42 times smaller than the headline.
method: Every figure in the 'measured' rows is read directly from verification/gpt6-comparison.json in openroboto-ai/jev-robot-control, pair 20260919-200239-715974-0, and divided. cost_usd and model_wait_seconds are per-run totals; api_calls is the per-run count of model requests. Per-call figures are total divided by api_calls. The repo's own offline verifier re-executes every recorded motor command in MuJoCo and reports max_qpos_error = 0.0 and cost_sum_verified = true for both arms. The last two rows invert the headline multiplier: they are the per-call LLM latency that would be required to reach 193.6x against Jev's measured latency in each of the two published harnesses.
source: openroboto-ai/jev-robot-control verification/gpt6-comparison.json and docs/RESULTS.md; browser-use/jev-ultrafast docs/performance.md; TypeSafe homepage figure as itemized in this site's earlier Jev piece.
note: This is ONE seed-0 trial per controller, which the repository states plainly and which is the reason it is evidence about magnitudes rather than a success rate. Both sides are remote HTTP endpoints over OpenRouter, so both latencies include a network round trip; that inflates Jev's absolute number and therefore makes the 4.57x ratio a conservative floor for Jev, not a ceiling. GPT-6 Astra ran at low reasoning effort with 4,096 max completion tokens — a long-reasoning-trace configuration would move the latency ratio up and is the only regime in which a three-figure speed multiplier is reachable.
